blocks.text: Take S = {(x,y) : x θ y}. This is a finite set because V is finite. Its defining property is (x,y) ∈ S if and only if x θ y.
blocks.title: Collect the related pairs

blocks.text: Choose a vertex v. Reflexivity gives v θ v, so (v,v) belongs to S. This supplies the nonempty-seed hypothesis of the graph condition.
blocks.title: The seed set is nonempty

blocks.text: Let λ be the join of c(x,y) over all pairs (x,y) in S. For arbitrary x and y, compare c(x,y) ≤ λ with x θ y. Establishing both implications identifies the threshold relation with θ.
blocks.title: Compare the relations

introduction: Let V be the finite, nonempty vertex set, let c be a lattice-valued coloring satisfying the graph-witness conditions, and let θ be a congruence of the algebra whose unary operations are all color-decreasing maps. We will express θ as a threshold relation: x θ y exactly when c(x,y) ≤ λ, for a suitable lattice element λ.
title: Every congruence is a color threshold
